meta.title: iOS Platform Support (F-10) — platform-dispatch seam + simctl/idb adapter

data.goal: Make PlatformModel.Ios a real, working branch of the existing Android mirror loop on the macOS desktop host: iOS simulator + physical-device discovery via xcrun simctl and idb, live screenshot-poll mirroring through the UNCHANGED ScreencapMirrorTransport, and the two already-drawn AC-31 error cards (simulator-not-booted, device-not-trusted) reachable for the first time. Hierarchy capture stays deferred to v1.1.
data.problemStatement: Picking iOS today kills the session and shows a static 'deferred' string (MirrorStage.IosDeferred) — no discovery, no mirroring, and the two drawn iOS error-card designs are unreachable. Worse, MirrorStageContent computes errorCard() BEFORE the stage `when` (MirrorContent.kt:124-128), errorCard() is platform-blind, and the discovery poll keeps issuing adb while iOS is selected — so picking iOS on a machine with no Android device renders the ANDROID 'no device' card. That shadowing bug must be fixed on both halves before any iOS error state can ever render. Underneath, the PRD's claim that 'only the device-adapter layer is new' is half true: DeviceRepository has no platform parameter, Koin binds one unqualified instance per datasource interface, adb is hardcoded in four load-bearing places (buildDeviceArgv's positional `-s`, DeviceCommand's literal adb shell lines, DeviceCommandExecutorImpl's unconditional ToolKind.Adb + poll()'s unconditional adbHostSource, and the unqualified Koin bindings), and ToolKind/DeviceCommand/HostCommand are documented closed sets. F-10 is therefore 'extract a dispatch seam, then add the actual'.
data.highLevelDescription: Two commits. COMMIT 1 is a pure refactor with ZERO iOS code: add `platform: PlatformModel` to exactly five DeviceRepository methods (observeDiscovery, mirror, dumpHierarchy, bootEmulator, observeMirrorStats) and let it ripple through 5 use-case interfaces, 5 use-case impls, MirrorViewModel, MirrorFakes and the four data-repository-impl device test files. DeviceRepositoryImpl accepts the parameter and ignores it; `git diff --word-diff` shows only `platform` insertions. The existing Android suite green IS AC-49. COMMIT 2 adds iOS: ToolKind.Simctl + widened DeviceCommand/HostCommand, a generalized buildDeviceArgv with a STRUCTURAL NFR-5 check, two hand-rolled parsers (parseSimctlDevices / parseIdbTargets), one IosHostSource replacing the deleted probe-only IdbHostSource, an IosDeviceCommandExecutor that maps the REUSED DeviceCommand.Screencap onto `xcrun simctl io <udid> screenshot --type=png -` / `idb screenshot --udid`, qualified named("android")/named("ios") Koin bindings for DeviceCommandExecutor and MirrorTransport only, DeviceRepositoryImpl's exhaustive `when` dispatch with poll() split into pollAndroid()/pollIos(), two new DiscoveryModel variants, the shadowing fix on both halves, the two MirrorErrorKind members with exactly ONE new intent (BootSimulator(udid)), and the picker relabel. ScreencapMirrorTransport and ProcessRunner are edited ZERO times.
data.background: F-2/F-3 shipped the Android device adapter with clean, already-neutral interfaces: DeviceCommandExecutor.run(DeviceId, DeviceCommand): ByteArray, MirrorTransport.frames(DeviceId): Flow<MirrorFrame> + stats, and a ScreencapMirrorTransport that depends only on DeviceCommandExecutor and never names adb. F-9 proved the whole measure/verify/diff stack below HierarchySnapshotModel is rect- and pixel-neutral. ProcessRunner is a single internal object with run()/spawnDetached() that knows nothing about adb. The missing piece is platform dispatch — which lives nowhere today. The iOS tooling probe (2026-10-19) measured this host: Xcode 26.3 (build 17C529) with runtimes iOS 17.5 and 18.1, idb at ~/.local/bin/idb, idb_companion at /opt/homebrew/bin/idb_companion, and NO simulator booted — which is the natural, free reproduction of AC-31's simulator-not-booted half.

in: COMMIT 1 — platform-dispatch extraction as a standalone pure refactor: `platform: PlatformModel` added to the five dispatching DeviceRepository methods (observeDiscovery, mirror, dumpHierarchy, bootEmulator, observeMirrorStats) and threaded through 5 use-case interfaces, 5 use-case impls, MirrorViewModel, MirrorFakes and four data-repository-impl test files. Zero iOS code, zero new tests, reviewable as a `git diff --word-diff` of `platform` insertions.

ToolKind.Simctl("xcrun", null); DeviceCommand.SimulatorBoot; HostCommand.{XcrunVersion, ListSimulators, IdbVersion, ListTargets} — each an explicit, KDoc-documented, visible API widening of a closed set.

buildDeviceArgv(tool, toolPath, device, command): per-ToolKind selector branch (adb `-s` prefix / simctl positional-after-subcommand / idb `--udid` suffix) followed by `check(argv.count { it == device.value } == 1)`, backed by an exhaustive ToolKind × DeviceCommand sweep test.

Hand-rolled parseSimctlDevices over `xcrun simctl list devices available` plain text and parseIdbTargets over `idb list-targets` pipe-split rows, with fixtures captured from THIS host (Xcode 26.3). No new dependency.
IosHostSource (probeSimctl/probeIdb/listSimulators/listDevices/bootSimulator) REPLACING the probe-only IdbHostSource, which is deleted along with IdbHostSourceImpl and UnsupportedIdbHostSource.
IosDeviceCommandExecutor dispatching the REUSED DeviceCommand.Screencap to simctl/idb; ScreencapMirrorTransport registered twice and edited zero times; ProcessRunner edited zero times.

Qualified named("android")/named("ios") Koin bindings for DeviceCommandExecutor and MirrorTransport ONLY, in the single existing seam DeviceSourcesProvider.desktop.kt, using explicit `single { get(named(...)) }` per koin-di.md.

DeviceRepositoryImpl: exhaustive `when (platform)` selection, poll() split into pollAndroid() (moved verbatim) and pollIos() (new), and the PollFailed catch's hardcoded ToolKind.Adb.binaryName fixed to name the platform's own tool.
DiscoveryModel.SimulatorNotBooted and DiscoveryModel.DeviceNotTrusted (unprefixed, SUCCESS values, never Failure).

Shadowing fix on BOTH halves: selectPlatform() cancels and re-collects the discovery job and resets discovery = Detecting / rows = emptyList(); errorCard() gains a platform guard returning null for Android-only variants when platform == Ios.
Deletion of MirrorStage.IosDeferred, its `platform == Ios -> IosDeferred` derivation branch, its render branch, and the mirror_ios_deferred string.

MirrorErrorKind.SimulatorNotBooted / DeviceNotTrusted with their MirrorErrorCard content and ~9 new strings; exactly ONE new intent, MirrorIntent.BootSimulator(udid); 'Choose another' and 'Use simulator' reuse OpenPicker, "I've tapped Trust — retry" reuses RetryDiscovery.
EmulatorModel.runningDeviceId carries the udid even for a SHUT-DOWN simulator (KDoc widened, no new field) because simulator names are not unique across runtimes.

Picker: platformCards()'s hardcoded `enabled = platform == Android` replaced; mirror_group_emulator relabelled to a platform-neutral value; MirrorRowGroup{Physical,Emulator} and MirrorRowKind.Boot reused unchanged.

Unsupported* stand-ins: UnsupportedIosHostSource added; the existing UnsupportedDeviceCommandExecutor / UnsupportedMirrorTransport registered under BOTH qualifiers so the Android and iOS app Koin graphs still resolve.
observeMirrorStats gains a simctlVersion field alongside adbVersion so the iOS status line is not blank.
out: iOS view-hierarchy capture / AX JSON parsing and the rawDump/hierarchyXml rename it would require — deferred to v1.1 (FR-57). iOS already degrades to "" for free via the Android-gated attachedHierarchyXml.

idb video-stream high-fps mirroring and the H.264/MJPEG decode it needs — it would require a second ProcessRunner entry point (stream(argv): Flow<ByteArray>) and a second transport, destroying the 'ScreencapMirrorTransport unchanged' saving. Screenshot polling only in v1.
:ios-application (the on-device Rectify app, an Xcode project not a Gradle module) — F-10 is a desktop-host capability per platform-coverage.md. Zero files touched there.
:compose-application — nothing testable may land there (it has no test wiring by design). RectifyWindow.kt's PLATFORM_SOURCES already lists iOS; no change needed.
Adding kotlinx-serialization-json to data-device-api — moot while hierarchy capture is deferred; `-j` JSON is the documented escape hatch, not this spec's path.
Simulator lifecycle beyond boot (create/delete/erase/reset), and auto-starting idb_companion — that is somebody else's daemon.
Renaming bootEmulator to bootTarget (6 files for zero behavioural value; KDoc carries the truth instead).
Platform-specific picker group wording ('Emulators' / 'Simulators') — needs a new DevicePickerPanel parameter for a cosmetic win; one neutral string ships instead.
A Compose UI-test harness. None exists in the repo; adopting one is its own infrastructure decision.

assumptions: AS-1 — A Mac host with Xcode command-line tools, simctl, idb and idb_companion installed is the only supported dev/build environment for F-10, consistent with NFR-10's macOS-only scope.

AS-2 — idb's list-targets output can distinguish booted/shutdown simulators and trusted/untrusted physical devices; the exact field/error signal for 'untrusted' is confirmed during implementation, contained in ONE named token set inside parseIdbTargets so it is correctable from one place.
AS-3 — No environment available to this project has a real untrusted iPhone; device-not-trusted coverage is accepted as fixture-driven per NFR-18 rather than blocking the feature.
AS-4 — Hierarchy capture on iOS is out of scope; the existing Android-gated attachedHierarchyXml behaviour (empty string on iOS) is sufficient and requires no change (FR-57).

PLAN-AS-1 — Preparation describes commit 1 as 'qualified Koin bindings + platform threaded through'. Those cannot both be zero-iOS-code: a named("ios") binding needs an iOS implementation to bind. This plan resolves it by putting ONLY the signature threading in commit 1 (which is what makes the word-diff claim literally true) and the qualifier registration in commit 2, where its sibling exists. Recorded as a deliberate deviation, not an omission.

PLAN-AS-2 — Preparation's '~45 files' estimate conflates the refactor ripple with the iOS work. Recounted against the real tree: the pure refactor is 19 files; the iOS commit is 47 file-level changes. Total ≈58 distinct files. The ~45 figure is not wrong in spirit; it is just not the refactor's number.

PLAN-AS-3 — A measured fixture of this host's `xcrun simctl list devices available` output does not exist yet. Capturing it is cheap, available now, and is a hard prerequisite for the parser tests (step 5).

constraints.text: iOS adapter classes are bound inside the existing desktopMain actual provideDeviceSources(); no new expect/actual is introduced. The repo's convention is expect/actual for the DI REGISTRATION FUNCTION only — plain interface + Koin binding for behaviour. There are no expect class datasources.

ToolKind/DeviceCommand/HostCommand widening must be an explicit, documented, visible API change per their existing KDoc contract. Reusing DeviceCommand.Screencap for iOS is honoured by REWRITING its KDoc to the platform-neutral meaning it already has ('capture the screen as an encoded PNG on stdout'), not by silently overloading an Android-shaped case.

buildDeviceArgv must keep enforcing the NFR-5 single-explicit-device invariant for every ToolKind including Simctl. The `check()` throwing IllegalStateException from a commonMain pure function is correct here and is NOT a mappers-never-throw violation: a selector-less argv is a programming error, unreachable from user data.

platform-coverage.md — ALL idb/simctl process invocation and every iOS datasource implementation lives exclusively under data-device-impl/src/desktopMain/. data-device-impl's commonMain names no java.* and no process API. Desktop here means the current-OS JVM target only; there is no macosMain.

error-handling.md — a missing tool or an empty device list is a SUCCESS value, never an exception. The iOS cards ride the MirrorErrorCard projection off DiscoveryModel, not Failure. Do NOT copy the recorded repo-wide gap where ShowError(messageId) handlers ignore messageId and show a hardcoded 'Error'.

The five external-process conventions hold unchanged: ONE process-starting site (ProcessRunner), closed DeviceCommand/HostCommand sets, ONE argv construction point enforcing the device selector, every budget named in MirrorTuning (no new tuning constants), and TIMEOUT_REASON_PREFIX shared producer↔consumer.

koin-di.md — one module per Gradle module, load order significant; provideDeviceSources() stays the single registration seam; qualified registrations use explicit `single<T>(named(...)) { ... get(named(...)) }` rather than singleOf.
package-layout.md + explicitApi() — core/ is internal-only, source/ is public with one subfolder per semantic concern, explicit visibility and explicit return types everywhere.

testing.md — the desktop target is the one that runs, but a cross-target build must pass before done: commonTest compiles for iosArm64 and Kotlin/Native rejects a backtick test name containing a comma or a colon (an apostrophe is fine, measured). Nothing testable may land in :compose-application, which has no test wiring by design.

mappers.md — Mapper<I,O> is a fun interface and a mapper NEVER throws; unknown values get a safe default in toModel. Both new parsers and SimulatorResourceMapper obey this: an unparseable line is skipped, never fatal.
Priority is `could`, phase PH-2, estimate L. The smallest scope satisfying AC-31/SC-14 is deliberately preferred over the full goal-statement parity list.
Effort tier fast; single drafter, no judge. The two-commit sequencing is the risk control that replaces a longer review cycle.

Whether idb_companion is RUNNING and whether idb is authorised against a physical device are separate, unprobed questions.

risks.text: AC-49 regression: the five-signature change ripples through ~19 files before any iOS behaviour exists. A mechanical edit at that scale is where a quiet behaviour change hides.
risks.mitigation: Land it as its own commit with ZERO iOS code and ZERO new tests. The only acceptable outcome is the existing Android suite green with DeviceRepositoryImpl's bodies untouched (commit 1 does not even split poll() — that happens in commit 2, where pollAndroid() is a verbatim MOVE). Review as a pure refactor; `git diff --word-diff` must show only `platform` insertions.

risks.text: `simctl list devices` plain-text format drifts with an Xcode release and parseSimctlDevices silently returns an empty list, rendering as 'no simulators' rather than a visible failure.
risks.mitigation: The parser never throws (repo convention), but pollIos() distinguishes 'command succeeded, zero rows parsed, NON-EMPTY stdout' and emits PollFailed(tool = "xcrun", reason = <stdout head>) instead of SimulatorNotBooted. That is the same NoDeviceFound-vs-PollFailed split DiscoveryModel already makes, and it makes drift visible. `-j` JSON is the documented escape hatch.

risks.text: `idb list-targets` hangs or fails without a running idb_companion, stalling the whole iOS poll once per interval.
risks.mitigation: Already budgeted by MirrorTuning.HostCommandTimeoutMs (3s). Additionally the idb call is wrapped so its failure yields an EMPTY physical list and never aborts the simctl half — simctl's simulator answer always survives. Deliberately no companion auto-start.

risks.text: Generalising buildDeviceArgv weakens NFR-5 — the security invariant this module exists to make unrepresentable.
risks.mitigation: This is the opposite of the usual 'we generalised and weakened an invariant' story and the plan says so explicitly. Today's guarantee is POSITIONAL (`listOf(toolPath, "-s", device.value) + command.arguments()`), enforced only by the shape of one line, and nothing stops a future arguments() branch appending a second target. After this spec it is STRUCTURAL: `check(argv.count { it == device.value } == 1)` plus an exhaustive ToolKind × DeviceCommand sweep asserting (a) argv[0] == toolPath, (b) the id appears exactly once, (c) no element matches the connect/-H/-P denylist. NFR-5 ends up STRONGER than before — provable by a test rather than by reading one line.

risks.text: Deleting MirrorStage.IosDeferred routes iOS through the full stage machine (Picker, Mirror, Frozen, Verify, NoSignal), exposing every stage to a platform none were written against.
risks.mitigation: That exposure IS the feature, and the stack below HierarchySnapshotModel is already rect/pixel-neutral (recon §6). The one iOS-shaped hole is hierarchy, which is Android-gated and degrades to "" — made an ASSERTED behaviour by AC-50's inspection step plus a test that fails if iOS ever starts returning nodes, rather than trusting the gate.

risks.text: iOS mirroring is materially slower than ~10fps and the feature ships feeling broken. `simctl io screenshot` plausibly costs 200–400 ms.
risks.mitigation: Measure once a simulator is booted and record the NUMBER in the verification table, the way CaptureFloorMs's waiver is recorded. Do NOT add an iOS tuning constant to paper over it. The adaptive single-flight loop degrades gracefully and TransportStats reports the truth. idb video-stream is the named upgrade path and is already out of scope.

risks.text: Scope creep back into hierarchy capture, because `idb ui describe-all` looks tantalisingly close once the adapter exists.
risks.mitigation: FR-57 and AC-50 make 'iOS returns an empty hierarchy' an asserted behaviour, not an omission. dumpHierarchy(Ios, …) short-circuits to HierarchySnapshotModel.Empty IN THE REPOSITORY without spawning a process and without throwing. A test that fails the moment iOS returns nodes is the cheapest guard.

risks.text: AS-2 unresolved: nobody has measured what `idb list-targets` prints for an untrusted physical iPhone, so DeviceNotTrusted's detection signal is a guess until measured.
risks.mitigation: Contain, do not guess. One named token set inside parseIdbTargets plus a fallback classifying a listed-but-unusable physical target as untrusted. Correctable from one place after a real measurement; the fixture test pins whatever is decided.

risks.text: No untrusted physical iPhone exists here (AS-3), and idb against a physical device has never been exercised on this host. AC-31's device-not-trusted half and the whole SC-26 physical path ship fixture-driven / code-review-verified only.
risks.mitigation: Write the waiver EXPLICITLY into the verification table rather than implying it; do not block the feature on it (NFR-18). AC-31's two halves are recorded separately so the simulator-not-booted measurement is never read as proving both.

risks.text: The qualified Koin bindings fail to resolve when the app runs on Android or iOS HARDWARE (not desktop) because UnsupportedDeviceSources does not register the qualifiers. This is not a desktop test failure — it is a startup crash on a phone.
risks.mitigation: FR-56: register the existing UnsupportedDeviceCommandExecutor / UnsupportedMirrorTransport under BOTH named("android") and named("ios"), add UnsupportedIosHostSource, remove UnsupportedIdbHostSource. Guard it with a Koin-graph resolution test in data-device-impl's desktopTest (DeviceSourcesModuleTest already exists for exactly this) and a cross-target build.

functional.text: (v1.1+) Support iOS simulator/device mirroring via idb+simctl, including simulator-not-booted and device-not-trusted error-card states.

Extract a platform-dispatch seam: thread `platform: PlatformModel` through DeviceRepository's methods (sourced from MirrorViewModel's existing state.platform) and register qualified Koin bindings (named("android") / named("ios")) for each of the five datasource interfaces in DeviceSourcesProvider.desktop.kt. PLAN REFINEMENT: `platform` lands on exactly the FIVE dispatching methods (observeDiscovery, mirror, dumpHierarchy, bootEmulator, observeMirrorStats); detectTools/refreshDiscovery/restartAdbServer/setAdbPath are deliberately unchanged. Qualifiers are registered for DeviceCommandExecutor and MirrorTransport ONLY — AdbHostSource, EmulatorSource and IosHostSource have one implementation each and stay unqualified.

Add a `ToolKind.Simctl` (xcrun-based) member and widen `DeviceCommand`/`HostCommand` with new iOS-shaped variants (screenshot, list simulators/devices, boot simulator) as an explicit, documented, visible API change; the sets otherwise stay closed. PLAN REFINEMENT: screenshot REUSES DeviceCommand.Screencap (its KDoc rewritten platform-neutral); the genuinely new members are DeviceCommand.SimulatorBoot and HostCommand.{XcrunVersion, ListSimulators, IdbVersion, ListTargets}.

Generalize `buildDeviceArgv` so the device-selector flag is chosen per `ToolKind` (adb `-s`, simctl `-u`, idb `--udid`) while preserving the NFR-5 invariant that the argv always embeds the one explicitly selected, connected device id. PLAN REFINEMENT: simctl's selector is POSITIONAL-AFTER-SUBCOMMAND (`simctl io <udid> screenshot …`), not `-u`; the invariant is re-expressed structurally rather than positionally.

Implement iOS discovery polling (booted/unbooted simulators and connected physical devices via idb/simctl) producing new DiscoveryModel variants for simulator-not-booted and device-not-trusted, replacing the current static MirrorStage.IosDeferred stage when platform == Ios.

Fix the errorCard() shadowing bug: the discovery poll stops issuing adb once platform == Ios (a direct consequence of FR-48's platform threading), and DiscoveryErrorProjection/errorCard() render the new iOS-specific DiscoveryModel variants instead of being shadowed by stale Android state.

Add `MirrorErrorKind.SimulatorNotBooted` and `MirrorErrorKind.DeviceNotTrusted` with their `MirrorErrorCard` content, new intents (BootSimulator, UseSimulator, RetryTrust, ChooseAnother) and MirrorViewModel wiring, satisfying AC-31. CONFIRMED BY SURVEY: only `MirrorIntent.BootSimulator(udid)` is genuinely new — 'Choose another' and 'Use simulator' both map to the existing `MirrorIntent.OpenPicker`, and "I've tapped Trust — retry" maps to the existing `MirrorIntent.RetryDiscovery` (which already cuts the poll interval short via refreshDiscovery). Implement ONE new intent plus two reused ones, not four distinct intent types.

Implement iOS live mirroring by generalizing DeviceCommandExecutor to dispatch iOS screenshot commands (`xcrun simctl io <udid> screenshot --type=png -` for simulators, `idb screenshot` for physical devices) and reusing `ScreencapMirrorTransport` unchanged.

Extend the device picker: reuse `MirrorRowGroup{Physical,Emulator}` and `MirrorRowKind.Boot` unchanged for iOS rows; replace `platformCards()`'s hardcoded `enabled = platform == Android`; relabel `mirror_group_emulator` to a platform-neutral string.

Add `Unsupported*` stand-ins for any newly introduced iOS-facing datasource surface so the Android/iOS app Koin graphs still resolve, per the existing iosMain stand-in convention (e.g. UnsupportedAdbHostSource).

Leave iOS view-hierarchy capture as today's no-op: `attachedHierarchyXml` stays Android-gated and `HierarchySnapshotModel.rawDump` remains "" on iOS — explicitly deferred to v1.1 per the scope decision below.

nonFunctional.text: adb/idb commands are only ever invoked against the user's explicitly selected, connected device — never an arbitrary or remote target. STRENGTHENED by this spec: today's guarantee is POSITIONAL (`listOf(toolPath, "-s", device.value) + command.arguments()`), enforced only by the shape of one line. After this spec it is STRUCTURAL — buildDeviceArgv builds the per-tool argv in a `when (tool)` (adb `-s` prefix / simctl positional-after-subcommand / idb `--udid` suffix) and then asserts `check(argv.count { it == device.value } == 1)` before returning, backed by an exhaustive ToolKind × DeviceCommand sweep test. This is the opposite of the usual 'we generalised and weakened an invariant' story — recorded explicitly, by instruction.

Device picker, annotation popovers, and error-card actions are fully keyboard-navigable (arrow keys/Enter for pickers, Enter/Escape for popovers). FREE for iOS: pickerKeyAction / nextSelectableIndex / the single onPreviewKeyEvent + FocusRequester path know nothing about adb and are platform-blind already.

All screens support full light and dark theme parity using the defined signal-color system (red = bug, green = fixed, orange = warning, blue = measurement) with sufficient contrast in both themes. FREE for iOS: the two new cards render through the existing ErrorCard organism with existing tokens; covered by @Preview pairs in light and dark, as every other card is.
v1 targets macOS only; no Windows/Linux builds.

AC-31's simulator-not-booted half must be verified against the real simctl/idb toolchain on a host with no booted simulator (measured feasible per ios-tooling-probe.md: no simulator booted, simctl and idb installed); the device-not-trusted half is permitted to be fake-driven via a constructed DiscoveryModel fixture — documented as a waiver since no untrusted physical iPhone is available in this environment.

All idb/simctl process invocation and iOS datasource implementations live exclusively under data-device-impl/src/desktopMain (per platform-coverage.md); commonMain stays free of java.* and process APIs, and :ios-application is untouched since F-10 is a desktop-host capability.

The platform-dispatch extraction (FR-48) must not change observable Android behavior — identical DiscoveryModel outputs, error cards, and mirroring characteristics — verified by the existing Android test suite remaining green (AC-49).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given iOS is selected as platform, when the simulator isn't booted, then an error card with 'Boot simulator' primary / 'Choose another' secondary renders; when the device isn't trusted, an error card with "I've tapped Trust — retry" primary / 'Use simulator' secondary renders. COVERAGE IS SPLIT AND MUST BE READ AS SPLIT: (a) simulator-not-booted is REAL and MEASURED on this host (no simulator booted at probe time; simctl and idb installed) — the projection assertion is pure commonTest and the underlying state is produced from real `xcrun simctl list devices available` output in the guarded desktopTest; (b) device-not-trusted is FIXTURE-DRIVEN and WAIVED per NFR-18/AS-3 — no untrusted physical iPhone exists here, so a constructed DiscoveryModel.DeviceNotTrusted drives the projection and nothing about real idb trust behaviour is proven. Do not let (a)'s measurement be read as covering (b).

Given iOS is selected and discovery runs, when no simulator is booted (measured on a real host via simctl/idb per ios-tooling-probe.md), then DiscoveryModel reflects the iOS-specific simulator-not-booted state and the Android 'no device' card does not render instead (shadowing fix verified).

Given iOS is selected and the error card shows 'Boot simulator', when the user clicks it, then the app invokes the simulator boot command for the selected simulator and discovery re-polls and surfaces it as selectable without an app restart.

Given iOS is selected and a simulator or trusted physical device is available, when mirroring starts, then live frames render through the generalized DeviceCommandExecutor/ScreencapMirrorTransport path with the same MirrorFrame contract (PNG bytes, width/height, fps stats) Android uses today.

Given the platform-dispatch extraction (threading `platform` through DeviceRepository + qualified Koin bindings) lands, when the existing Android device-discovery/mirroring/error-card test suite runs, then every existing Android test still passes with no behavior change.

Given iOS is selected, when a view-hierarchy dump is requested, then the app returns the same empty hierarchy (rawDump "") it returns today, confirming hierarchy capture is deliberately deferred with no regression and no new wire-field rename.

architecture.approach: Keep every existing interface and every existing transport/process primitive. Add `platform: PlatformModel` to exactly the five DeviceRepository methods that genuinely dispatch, resolve per-platform implementations through qualified Koin bindings inside the ONE existing registration seam (DeviceSourcesProvider.desktop.kt), and let DeviceRepositoryImpl select with an exhaustive `when` (compile-time totality, not a map lookup). Sequence it as two commits: a pure signature refactor with zero iOS code, then the iOS adapter.
architecture.rationale: Dispatch becomes explicit at the type level — a reader of `mirror(platform, id)` sees which device family it targets. ScreencapMirrorTransport is reused VERBATIM as two Koin instances, so 'iOS mirroring' at the transport layer is zero new code; that is the single largest saving in the spec and the reason screenshot polling beat idb video-stream. There is no hidden mutable platform state in the data layer, so MirrorViewModel's state.platform stays the single source of truth. And `observeDiscovery(platform)` being a PARAMETERISED flow is what forces the adb loop to actually stop when the user switches — fixing half the shadowing bug by construction rather than by a flag check. The honest cost is 19 mechanical files before any iOS behaviour exists; the diff is a signature change with no logic change, which is exactly what makes the existing Android suite a real regression guard rather than a formality.

alternativesConsidered.title: Dispatching decorator over a StateFlow<PlatformModel>
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Far smaller diff (no DeviceRepository signature changes, AC-49 nearly free) but it hides platform in mutable shared state: `mirror(deviceId)` reads one thing today and another after a toolbar click with no signature to show it. It introduces a race invisible in the types — a mirror() call in flight while the platform flips targets the wrong tool — and still needs a setter path from the ViewModel, so the 'no call sites change' saving is partly illusory. Smaller now, worse at 3am. Explicitly rejected by the confirmed clarify survey.

alternativesConsidered.title: A single PlatformDeviceSource super-interface collapsing all five datasources into one per platform
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: The textbook-prettiest option and the worst fit for a `could`-priority feature whose headline constraint is 'do not change Android behaviour'. It forces a lowest-common-denominator shape on surfaces that genuinely differ (adb has a daemon lifecycle, simctl has none; emulator boot is a detached foreground process, simctl boot is not), rewrites the Android path wholesale putting NFR-20/AC-49 at real risk, and deletes the fine-grained test fakes four test files depend on.

alternativesConsidered.title: `simctl list devices -j` (JSON) instead of plain text
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: data-device-api has zero dependencies beyond :data-core and no serialization plugin, so JSON means adding kotlinx-serialization-json for one list of three fields, or hand-rolling a JSON reader. It also contradicts the confirmed clarify answer 'Moot — no JSON parsing needed in v1'. The plain-text rows are regex-shaped and match parseAdbDevices' precedent exactly. `-j` is kept as the documented escape hatch and becomes the right answer the day v1.1 hierarchy capture needs real JSON anyway.

alternativesConsidered.title: `idb video-stream` for mirroring
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Higher fps, but it needs a second ProcessRunner entry point (run() buffers stdout to EOF), H.264/MJPEG decode that decodeToImageBitmap() cannot do against a contractually-PNG MirrorFrame.bytes, and a second transport implementation — destroying the 'ScreencapMirrorTransport unchanged' saving. Revisit only if measured iOS screenshot latency proves 10fps unusable.

alternativesConsidered.title: Add `EmulatorModel.bootId: String?` to carry a shut-down simulator's udid
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Honest but structural: a new field on a shared domain model for one platform's identifier quirk, plus matching reads in DiscoveryProjection.toRow and anywhere else that builds a boot target. Populating the existing runningDeviceId with the udid even when shut down (KDoc widened) is zero structural change and produces exactly the right row — id = udid, serial = udid, kind = Boot driven by isRunning. Add the real field the day a second consumer keys 'is running' off `runningDeviceId != null`.

alternativesConsidered.title: Add DeviceCommand.IosScreenshot as a distinct member
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: It would force a platform-aware branch INSIDE ScreencapMirrorTransport — the one file this spec most wants to leave alone. Reusing Screencap (same semantics: 'capture the screen as an encoded PNG on stdout'; only the argv differs per ToolKind) is precisely what makes the transport reusable verbatim. The 'no silent overloading' constraint is honoured by rewriting Screencap's KDoc to the platform-neutral meaning it already had.

alternativesConsidered.title: Rename bootEmulator to bootTarget
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Touches 6 files for zero behavioural value and inflates the AC-49 regression surface. The KDoc carries the truth instead. Revisit if a third platform ever lands.

alternativesConsidered.title: Platform-specific picker group labels ('Emulators' / 'Simulators')
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Needs a new parameter on the shipped DevicePickerPanel organism for a cosmetic win. One neutral string ('Virtual devices') ships instead; the pair is the noted upgrade path.

errorStates.behavior: DiscoveryModel.Detecting while the first iOS poll is in flight. selectPlatform() resets to Detecting on every switch so the user never sees the previous platform's answer attributed to the new one.

No simulators and no physical devices at all -> DiscoveryModel.NoDeviceFound with iOS-worded copy. Distinct from SimulatorNotBooted, which means 'simulators exist but none is running'. Both are success values.

SIMULATOR NOT BOOTED (err-sim) — simctl lists simulators but none is Booted. MirrorErrorKind.SimulatorNotBooted; primary 'Boot simulator' -> MirrorIntent.BootSimulator(udid from MirrorErrorCard.primaryDeviceId); secondary 'Choose another' -> MirrorIntent.OpenPicker. Recovers without an app restart (AC-47).

DEVICE NOT TRUSTED (err-trust) — a physical iPhone is the ONLY candidate and is listed-but-unusable. MirrorErrorKind.DeviceNotTrusted; primary "I've tapped Trust — retry" -> MirrorIntent.RetryDiscovery (already cuts the poll interval short); secondary 'Use simulator' -> MirrorIntent.OpenPicker. If a booted simulator ALSO exists, Found wins and the untrusted device shows as a disabled row with its state verbatim — exactly how parseAdbDevices treats an `unauthorized` handset.

TOOL MISSING — xcrun present but simctl absent (Command Line Tools without full Xcode: `xcrun: error: unable to find utility "simctl"`). Probing the xcrun BINARY alone is not sufficient; probeSimctl() verifies the subcommand resolves and reports ToolMissing with the 'xcode-select --install' hint rather than failing at first use. The iOS card never offers 'Restart adb' or 'Locate adb…'.

POLL FAILED — parser drift. simctl exits zero, stdout is non-empty, and parseSimctlDevices returns zero rows: emit PollFailed(tool = "xcrun", reason = <stdout head>), NOT SimulatorNotBooted. Makes an Xcode format change visible instead of silently rendering 'no simulators'.

IDB UNAVAILABLE — `idb list-targets` fails or times out (no idb_companion running). Budgeted by MirrorTuning.HostCommandTimeoutMs; the failure degrades the PHYSICAL list to empty and never aborts the simctl half, so simulators still render. No companion auto-start.

SIMULATOR DIES MID-STREAM — `simctl io screenshot` exits non-zero; DeviceCommandException propagates through the unchanged transport and flips the session to Lost, identical to an unplugged Android handset. Zero new code.

ALREADY BOOTED — `simctl boot <udid>` exits non-zero with 'Unable to boot device in current state: Booted'. Treated as SUCCESS: the user's goal is achieved. This is why boot uses run() rather than spawnDetached — the exit code matters.

MULTIPLE DEVICES — a booted simulator AND a trusted physical iPhone both present yields Found with ≥2 selectable physical rows and the existing MultipleDevices card. Correct and already handled; zero iOS work.

HIERARCHY ON iOS — dumpHierarchy(Ios, …) short-circuits to HierarchySnapshotModel.Empty in the repository WITHOUT spawning a process and WITHOUT throwing. attachedHierarchyXml stays Android-gated so the prompt degrades to "" exactly as today (FR-57, AC-50).

logs: DeviceCommandException(argv, exitCode, stderrTail) from ProcessRunner remains the single diagnostic record for every failed simctl/idb invocation, with the TIMEOUT_REASON_PREFIX discriminator unchanged.

PollFailed(tool, reason) now reports the PLATFORM'S OWN binary name instead of the hardcoded ToolKind.Adb.binaryName — on iOS that means 'xcrun' or 'idb', surfaced verbatim in the error card's diagnostic line.
Parser-drift signal: 'simctl succeeded, zero rows parsed, non-empty stdout' is logged into PollFailed's reason as the stdout head so an Xcode format change is diagnosable from the card itself.

dataHandling: NFR-5 moves from a POSITIONAL guarantee to a STRUCTURAL one. Today `listOf(toolPath, "-s", device.value) + command.arguments()` is enforced only by the shape of one line, and nothing stops a future arguments() branch appending a second target. After this spec, buildDeviceArgv builds per-tool in a `when (tool)` and then asserts `check(argv.count { it == device.value } == 1)` before returning. Tool-agnostic, fails loudly for any branch that forgets or duplicates the selector, and machine-checked by an exhaustive ToolKind × DeviceCommand sweep. NFR-5 ends up STRONGER after this spec than before it.

The sweep test asserts three properties per pair: argv[0] == toolPath, the device id appears exactly once, and no element matches the connect/-H/-P denylist (no remote or arbitrary target can be addressed).

DeviceId keeps its private constructor and DeviceCommand/HostCommand stay closed sets, so the argv remains unforgeable from user data. `check()` throwing IllegalStateException from a commonMain pure function is correct here — a selector-less argv is a programming error, not unexpected input, and must never be reachable from user input.
All process invocation stays behind ONE site (ProcessRunner), unchanged. No new process-starting code is introduced anywhere.
Screenshot bytes stay in memory and flow through the existing MirrorFrame path; iOS adds no new persistence, no new file write and no new network call.
permissions: No new OS permission is requested. simctl operates on the user's own simulators; idb requires the user to have trusted this Mac on the physical device — the untrusted case is precisely the error state this spec surfaces rather than a permission to request.
idb_companion is NOT auto-started. It is the user's daemon; the app reports its absence (degraded physical list) rather than spawning it.
privacy: Device udids and simulator names appear in the picker, the status line and error-card diagnostics — the same visibility level adb serials already have. Nothing is transmitted off-host.

Carry-over from the Android feature's recorded SEC-1: DeviceCommand.GetProp takes unvalidated free text into an adb shell (no production callers). The sweep test adds the first machine-checked guard over that family — see knownRisksFromQA.

rollout.backwardCompatibility: No persisted-data or wire-format change. AnnotationEnvelope's field order (wire-breaking) is untouched; hierarchyXml keeps its name because hierarchy capture is deferred (FR-57) — that rename is explicitly NOT paid for here. No Room migration. The only breaking changes are SOURCE-level and internal to this repo: DeviceRepository's five signatures (ripples into 5 use-case interfaces and their impls), buildDeviceArgv's signature (one Android call site), DeviceCommandExecutorImpl renamed to AdbDeviceCommandExecutor (one import site), and the deletion of IdbHostSource/IdbHostSourceImpl/UnsupportedIdbHostSource/MirrorStage.IosDeferred/mirror_ios_deferred. All are compile-time visible — explicitApi() and the exhaustive `when` over PlatformModel make an unhandled case a compile error, not a runtime surprise. Rollout is a straight merge; the two-commit split is the risk control, not a flag.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Kotlin/Native release linker OOMs under ~4 parallel linkReleaseFramework tasks (Java heap space against a 4 GiB daemon heap). Pre-existing, affects EVERY cross-target gate in this repo.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The mandated cross-target build (`:data-device-api:build :data-repository-impl:build :presentation-feature-mirror:build`) failing with 'Java heap space' rather than a real compile error — easy to misread as this spec's bug.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Run the cross-target gate with `--max-workers=1`, the documented workaround used for every cross-target gate on the previous spec. Do not chase a phantom iOS compile failure.

knownRisksFromQA.description: EmulatorModel.toRow sets no detail, unlike DeviceModel.toRow — an information gap in the device picker. Located in presentation-feature-mirror/core/discovery/DiscoveryProjection.kt, which this spec edits.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: iOS simulator rows inheriting the same blank detail, so the picker shows 'iPhone 16' twice with no runtime ('iOS 18.1') to disambiguate — which matters MORE on iOS than Android because simulator names are NOT unique across runtimes.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Do not fix PP-TD-9 here (it belongs to android-device-discovery-mirroring and its own gate), but DO populate the iOS simulator row's detail with the runtime so the duplicate-name case is distinguishable. That is additive and does not touch the Android branch. Flag the Android half as still open.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Tautological test: assertEquals(1, PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION) — asserts a literal against itself and would pass under any edit.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The same failure mode in this spec's new tests: asserting that ToolKind.Simctl.binaryName == "xcrun" or that DiscoveryModel.SimulatorNotBooted exists proves nothing. The argv sweep and the parser fixtures must assert BEHAVIOUR against real captured output.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Every new test must be falsifiable by a deliberate mutation. For the argv sweep, verify by temporarily deleting the selector from one branch and confirming the sweep goes red.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Test name and comment claim a structural property the body does not assert (body asserts Empty -> empty twice). Same self-referential failure mode that produced three defects on that spec.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: AC-50's 'iOS returns an empty hierarchy' test degenerating into asserting Empty == Empty. It must assert that dumpHierarchy(Ios, …) returns Empty WITHOUT the executor being called — a fake executor that fails the test if invoked is the real assertion.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Write the AC-50 test against a fake DeviceCommandExecutor whose run() throws; the test passes only because the repository never reaches it.

knownRisksFromQA.description: core/payload file names do not partition their contents (one label function in one file while two live in another).
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The same drift in the new iOS files: parseSimctlDevices and parseIdbTargets each getting their own file is correct; resisting the temptation to dump both plus the two resources into one IosParsers.kt.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: One concern per file, matching the existing AdbDevicesParser.kt / AvdListParser.kt / WmOutputParser.kt partition exactly.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Android capture rate was never measured (handset unauthorized, AVD never booted), so MirrorTuning.CaptureFloorMs stays at an UNMEASURED 100ms and latency is reported as an explicit placeholder rather than a fabricated figure.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: SC-25's success metric ('iOS reaches the same ~10fps floor as Android') being read as a comparison against a measured Android baseline. There is no measured Android baseline. Also watch for the temptation to report a fabricated iOS latency — TransportStats.latencyMs is null BY DESIGN.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Record the measured iOS captureRoundTripMs as a raw number with the explicit note that the Android comparison point is itself unmeasured. Do not fabricate latency.

knownRisksFromQA.description: DeviceCommand.GetProp takes unvalidated free text into an adb shell (no production callers today).
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: The buildDeviceArgv generalisation being the moment that free text reaches a NEW tool. GetProp has no iOS meaning and must throw a documented DeviceCommandException on an iOS tool rather than being quietly argv-built.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: The exhaustive ToolKind × DeviceCommand sweep covers the GetProp × Simctl and GetProp × Idb pairs explicitly, asserting the documented throw. This spec adds the first machine-checked guard over that family without taking on the Android-side fix.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Every feature's XSideEffect.ShowError(messageId) handler IGNORES messageId and shows a hardcoded, unlocalized 'Error' title. Explicitly documented as a gap, NOT a pattern to extend.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: Routing an iOS failure through ShowError instead of the MirrorErrorCard projection, which would both lose the message and copy the gap.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: By construction: a missing tool and an empty device list are SUCCESS values on DiscoveryModel and ride the error-card projection. No new ShowError call site is added by this spec.

knownRisksFromQA.description: resultLauncher catches CancellationException — an inherited open change request carried across four specs, still unfixed.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: selectPlatform()'s NEW discovery-job cancellation producing a swallowed CancellationException that surfaces as a spurious Failure instead of a clean stop when the user flips platforms mid-poll.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: Cancel the collection JOB in the ViewModel (outside the use case's resultLauncher scope) rather than cancelling inside the flow, and add an explicit test that a platform switch mid-poll leaves state at Detecting with no error side effect. Do not attempt the repo-wide resultLauncher fix here.

knownRisksFromQA.description: Cmd+1/2/3 LIVE dispatch is unverifiable; only the pure shortcutToTab mapping is tested. The precedent: live keyboard dispatch in this shell is not machine-verified.
knownRisksFromQA.watchFor: Claiming NFR-8 keyboard coverage for the new iOS picker rows on the strength of PickerNavigationTest alone. That test covers the pure arithmetic, not live dispatch.
knownRisksFromQA.mitigation: State NFR-8's iOS coverage as 'pure navigation logic tested, live dispatch unverified — same standing as Android', not as newly proven.
